title: The Scramble for Europe. Russia, China, and Turkey Challenging Regional Order
gist: Book announcement for Dimitar Bechev's The Scramble for Europe (Oxford University Press), which argues the EU-anchored European regional order has been in crisis since the late 2000s and is being challenged by Russia, China, Turkey and increasingly the U.S., each with distinct objectives. Russia pursues radical revisionism, China seeks to co-opt a diminished Europe economically, and Turkey wants recognition as a top-tier European stakeholder rather than a perpetual EU candidate.

insights.claim: Dimitar Bechev argues that Europe has shifted from being a global agenda-setter to being on the back foot, squeezed by internal populism and external pressure from Russia, China, Turkey and the United States that undermines EU cohesion and influence.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: A less cohesive EU implies weaker collective bargaining power on trade, sanctions and regulation, raising policy risk for European assets.
insights.quote: Europe used to be an agenda-setter at the global level but is now on the backfoot, facing rising populism internally as well as pressures from Russia, China, Turkey, and the U.S.

insights.claim: Bechev dates the crisis of the EU-anchored European regional order to the late 2000s, following an earlier period of consolidation.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Frames current European fragmentation as a structural, multi-decade trend rather than a cyclical shock.
insights.quote: traces the consolidation and, starting from the late 2000s, the subsequent crisis of the European regional order anchored in the EU

insights.claim: Reviewer Charles King says Europe now faces, more than at any point since modern European integration began, a combination of internal challenges and strategic competitors, including increasingly the United States, whose interests run counter to continent-wide cooperation.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Listing the U.S. among challengers signals transatlantic divergence as a live risk factor for European defense and trade policy.
insights.quote: the continent now faces a perfect storm of internal challenges and strategic competitors - Russia, China, Turkey, and increasingly the United States - whose interests run counter to continent-wide cooperation

insights.claim: Bechev argues that authoritarian powers are directly challenging the EU-anchored European order and seeking to remake Europe in their own image, though their objectives differ.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Differentiated challenger strategies require differentiated risk models rather than a single 'authoritarian threat' lens.
insights.quote: He argues that authoritarian powers are posing a direct challenge to the latter as they seek to remake Europe in their image. At the same time, their objectives differ.

insights.claim: According to Bechev, Russia's invasion of Ukraine displayed a radical revisionist agenda toward the European order.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Implies the Russia-Europe confrontation is about order itself, supporting sustained defense spending and sanctions rather than a quick normalization.
insights.quote: The Ukraine invasion put on display Russia's radical revisionist agenda.

insights.claim: Bechev argues China aims to co-opt a diminished Europe, largely through economic means, into a future world order that China dominates.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Economic dependence on China (trade, inputs, investment) is the main channel of Chinese leverage over Europe, relevant to de-risking and trade-defense policy.
insights.quote: China aims to co-opt a diminished Europe, largely through economic means, in a future world order that it dominates.

insights.claim: Bechev argues Erdogan's Turkey wants a deal recognizing it as a top-tier stakeholder in Europe rather than remaining an eternal candidate for EU membership.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Points to a transactional EU-Turkey relationship outside the accession track, relevant to migration, defense-industrial and customs-union negotiations.
insights.quote: Erdogan's Turkey wants to strike a deal where it is recognized as a top-tier stakeholder in Europe, as opposed to an eternal candidate for EU membership.

insights.claim: Reviewer Happymon Jacob characterizes the three challengers' methods as Russia's brute force, China's economic gravitational pull, and Turkey's imperial reinvention.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Useful shorthand to map each challenger to a distinct risk channel: military, economic, and regional-influence.
insights.quote: Russia's brute force, China's economic gravitational pull, and Turkey's imperial reinvention are reshaping a regional order that once looked permanent

insights.claim: Reviewer Nathalie Tocci notes that, so far, the outcome of Europe's transformation under these external challenges defies the pessimistic views common in European debates.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Cautions against pricing in a European decline narrative too aggressively.
insights.quote: the outcome, so far, defies the conveniently pessimistic views often heard in European debates today
